findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes asynchronously and never awaited
findings.body: In the `allRemainingBookings` path, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an async callback inside forEach. The push into `apiDeletes` happens only after the await, i.e. on a later microtask/macrotask tick, while the surrounding handler continues and reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before the forEach callbacks have pushed anything. Previously (with the sync `getCalendar`) the deleteEvent promise was pushed synchronously and thus awaited. As a result, cancellation of all remaining recurring events returns success while the external calendar-event deletions are still in flight (or may never complete if the request/process ends), leaving orphaned events on users' calendars.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and the try/catch dead
findings.body: The change from `forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` means the returned promises are discarded: `Reschedule` returns and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` runs without waiting for the external calendar deletions, and the surrounding `try { ... } catch` can never catch rejections from the async callbacks (they become unhandled promise rejections). If the serverless function is frozen/terminated after the response, calendar events and video meetings for the rescheduled booking may never be deleted. The callbacks should be collected and awaited via Promise.all. Same issue exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so the appStore is not actually lazy and failures become unhandled rejections
findings.body: `const appStore = { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }` calls `import()` at module-evaluation time for every app. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR (async/lazy imports): merely importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading of all ~28 app packages. Worse, if any single app module throws at load time, its promise rejects with no `.catch` anywhere, producing an unhandled promise rejection at startup (a hard crash under Node's default behavior). To be lazy, the store should expose getters or functions (e.g. `get applecalendar() { return import("./applecalendar") }`) so imports only run on access.
